datasets.name: geoBoundaries South Africa ADM2 (district municipalities)
datasets.role: Municipal boundary for spatially explicit aggregation
datasets.spatial_coverage: South Africa, ADM2; one feature extracted for eThekwini
known_gaps: Ward (ADM4) polygons are not published at this level; ward-level results are blocked
Boundary vintage 2020 may not match the Census 2022 ward geography
Source is a redistribution of MDB data, not the MDB release itself
processing_steps: Downloaded the ADM2 GeoJSON for ZAF from the geoBoundaries API
Extracted the single feature whose name contains 'eThekwini'
Validated geometry validity and computed area in EPSG:32736 (2,556.6 km2)
Wrote a normalised FeatureCollection with source, licence and vintage recorded

datasets.name: geoBoundaries South Africa ADM4 (wards)
datasets.role: Ward geometry for spatially explicit candidate-level results
datasets.spatial_coverage: South Africa, ADM4; 110 eThekwini wards extracted
known_gaps: Redistribution of MDB data, not the MDB release itself
Official ward codes are not carried; ward numbers are parsed from the feature name (eThekwini 001)
Vintage 2020 may not match Census 2022 ward geography; a crosswalk to census geography is still required
Ward layer tiles the municipality exactly (area difference 0.0 km2) but has not been reconciled against an independent ward list
processing_steps: Downloaded the ADM4 GeoJSON for ZAF from the geoBoundaries API
Selected the 110 features whose name begins with 'eThekwini'
Parsed ward numbers from the feature name and recorded the provenance of that code
Validated geometry validity, containment and area reconciliation against the ADM2 municipality
Persisted ward geometry and a ward-to-municipality crosswalk in the boundary tables

datasets.name: Daily maximum temperature, Open-Meteo archive (ERA5-derived)
datasets.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Open-Meteo); underlying reanalysis: Copernicus ERA5
datasets.crs: EPSG:4326 (point locations reported by the source)
datasets.native_resolution: 0.25 deg (~28 km), 5 grid points returned for eThekwini
known_gaps: Secondary distribution of ERA5, not the Copernicus CDS product itself; CDS adapter not implemented
0.25 deg resolution cannot resolve ward-level differences; results are reported per grid cell
Returned grid coordinates are snapped by the provider and are not exact 0.25 deg multiples
No missing days reported for this period; gap-filling behaviour of the provider is undocumented
The most recent 2-3 months of this feed are preliminary ERA5T and can be revised; the window ends at the last complete calendar year to stay outside that revision range (ADR-008)
processing_steps: Selected grid cells intersecting the eThekwini boundary
Requested daily temperature_2m_max for each cell, 1980-2025, local-day timezone
Recorded the provider's reported latitude/longitude as the data location
Stored raw JSON payloads immutably, then wrote a canonical Parquet table
Enforced unique (cell_id, date) and numeric coercion of missing values

datasets.name: Municipal Demarcation Board ward boundaries
datasets.role: Authoritative ward geography for candidate-level results
datasets.licence: unknown — to be confirmed from the MDB release
datasets.spatial_coverage: national; ward subset for eThekwini required

Wards are currently sourced from the geoBoundaries ADM4 redistribution (see geoboundaries_zaf_adm4)
Release vintage must be matched to Census 2022 ward geography before any census join
Replace the substitute layer when the MDB release is reachable

Adapter contract declared in src/climate_resilience/ingestion/cds_era5.py; not exercised

datasets.name: Statistics South Africa Census 2022
datasets.licence: Statistics South Africa copyright; use permitted with acknowledgement
datasets.native_resolution: ward or main-place, to be confirmed
known_gaps: Ward-level socio-economic indicators (water, sanitation, tenure, employment) are published only through the interactive SuperWeb/SuperCross tools; no bulk file is available
The downloadable ward product covers population by age, sex and population group only
Census 2022 has 111 eThekwini wards; the ADM4 boundary layer has 110, so no ward-level join is performed
Stats SA HTML pages sit behind a bot challenge; direct file URLs work, but there is no stable landing page for automated retrieval
Small-cell suppression rules must be applied before publishing ward statistics

datasets.name: Census 2022 ward-level small area population estimates
datasets.role: Exposure denominator sensitivity; not a vulnerability source
datasets.licence: Statistics South Africa copyright; use permitted with acknowledgement of Stats SA as the source
known_gaps: Population only (age, sex, population group); no service, tenure or employment variables
111 eThekwini ward codes (59500001-59500111) vs 110 ADM4 polygons; the table is deliberately not joined to geometry
Small-area estimates, not direct census counts; Stats SA applies raking and suppression
Ward boundaries are the 2020 demarcation, not necessarily the ADM4 substitute geometry
processing_steps: Downloaded the Stats SA ward product zip containing three workbooks
Parsed population group, sex and age sheets; validated ward codes and cross-tab totals
Filtered to the eThekwini prefix 595 and derived ward_number from the official code
Stored the table with official codes and did not join it to boundary polygons

datasets.name: WorldPop 2020 UN-adjusted 1 km aggregated population
datasets.units: persons per 1 km cell (allocated by area share)
datasets.native_resolution: 1 km (~0.00833 deg); 100 m product not used (ADR-009)
datasets.spatial_coverage: South Africa; 3,654 cells clipped to eThekwini
known_gaps: 1 km product, not the 100 m dasymetric surface specified for production; the 100 m national GeoTIFF is 609 MB and the server does not support range requests (ADR-009)
2020 estimate is two years before Census 2022; totals differ from census counts
UN-adjusted to national estimates, so subnational totals are modelled rather than observed
Allocation to wards by 1 km cell area share; boundary cells are split, not reallocated to a finer grid
processing_steps: Downloaded the national 1 km UN-adjusted aggregated GeoTIFF (7.3 MB)
Read the eThekwini bounding-box window and validated EPSG:4326 and a single band
Masked nodata and allocated each cell's population by the cell's area share inside the municipality
Wrote a canonical parquet of 3,654 cells; ward allocation is a separate build step
